juice_unsafe.name: OWASP Juice Shop (unsafe config)
juice_unsafe.note: NODE_ENV=unsafe loads config/unsafe.yml (challenges.safetyMode=disabled). Docker-disabled challenges (restfulXssChallenge, httpHeaderXssChallenge) are then active; verified against build/models/product.js and build/routes/saveLoginIp.js. Admin session admin@juice-sh.op / admin123.

dvwa.name: Damn Vulnerable Web Application
dvwa.start: docker network create dvwa-net; docker run -d --name dvwa-db --network dvwa-net -e MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD=rootpass -e MARIADB_DATABASE=dvwa -e MARIADB_USER=dvwa -e MARIADB_PASSWORD=p@ssw0rd mariadb:11; docker run -d --name dvwa-official --network dvwa-net -p 127.0.0.1:8080:80 -e DB_SERVER=dvwa-db -e DEFAULT_SECURITY_LEVEL=low ghcr.io/digininja/dvwa@sha256:1af2cedda7617e4d22937e61c98bbf71d8b74b98e46f5e41dd6aa0a5183311b0
dvwa.note: login admin/password; security level forced to low via security.php. The digest is the real pin; the :latest tag is only what was pulled.

cases.source: Same sink as localXssChallenge; script-via-innerHTML is inert, but the attacker controls the string and can swap the carrier
cases.evidence: Playwright Chromium, 2026-11-02: 0 dialogs for THIS payload; the endpoint stays vulnerable (official challenge)
cases.note: endpoint-level ground truth: an inert payload does not make a live sink safe; the browser carrier arm is allowed to prove the sink with a different carrier

cases.evidence: No attacker-controlled input in the page
JSON response, no HTML execution context
JSON answer has no matching product and never renders the query as HTML
cases.note: payload-carrying control: a reflection in JSON is not XSS

blocked_tools.dalfox: requires an authenticated API write followed by an SPA product-dialog render; dalfox has a body injector but no authenticated write/render workflow
blocked_tools.nuclei: requires an authenticated PUT /api/Products/:id followed by SPA rendering; DAST templates have no write workflow

cases.evidence: Independent Playwright Chromium, 2026-11-03: PUT /api/Products/1 description=<iframe src=javascript:alert(`xss`)>, then /#/search?q=Apple + product-card click -> dialog 'xss' captured
cases.note: persisted description; the view is an Angular dialog opened by clicking the product card

blocked_tools.dalfox: requires an authenticated GET /rest/saveLoginIp with a persisted request header and an SPA render; there is no header-injection workflow in dalfox's URL scanner
blocked_tools.nuclei: requires an authenticated saveLoginIp header write plus SPA rendering of /#/privacy-security/last-login-ip

cases.evidence: Independent Playwright Chromium, 2026-11-03: GET /rest/saveLoginIp with True-Client-IP=<iframe src=javascript:alert(`xss`)>, fresh login (JWT snapshots lastLoginIp), then /#/privacy-security/last-login-ip -> dialog 'xss' captured
cases.note: the value is snapshotted into the JWT at login; a re-login after the write is mandatory (the tool's --stored-relogin)

cases.source: Same PUT endpoint as restfulXssChallenge, read back as JSON
cases.evidence: Independent Playwright/requests, 2026-11-03: response is application/json and contains the payload string; it is never parsed as HTML by the SPA
cases.note: stored-payload-in-JSON control: a JSON echo must not be reported as XSS

cases.evidence:

blocked_tools.nuclei: the guestbook write is a POST form; the DAST xss templates only fuzz GET parameters, so they never reach this sink

cases.source: DVWA vulnerabilities/xss_s/source/low.php (INSERT INTO guestbook + echo without escaping)
cases.evidence: Independent Playwright Chromium, 2026-11-03: POST txtName=xssprobe&mtxMessage=<script>alert(1)</script>&btnSign=Sign Guestbook, then GET the guestbook page -> dialog '1' captured
No attacker-controlled input; static welcome text
